verdict.rationale: uv is a local CLI. The main data it retains is its global dependency cache, and the docs give a first-party deletion control: `uv cache clean` clears the cache entirely or for a specific package. `--refresh` forces revalidation of cached data. Nothing in the evidence covers retention policies, such as automatic expiry, size limits or scheduled pruning, and nothing addresses privacy-oriented data handling. missing for 10: configurable retention or expiry policies, automatic or scheduled pruning, documentation framing data handling from a privacy standpoint, independent corroboration of deletion behavior.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can control data retention and deletion

citations.quote: To clear the cache entirely, run `uv cache clean`. To clear the cache for a specific package, run `uv cache clean <package-name>`.
uv uses aggressive caching to avoid re-downloading (and re-building) dependencies that have already been accessed in prior runs.
To force uv to revalidate cached data for all dependencies, pass `--refresh` to any command
